questions.prompt: Classify \(9\) kg, \(9\) N east, and \(9\) m as scalars or vectors.
questions.answer: \(9\) kg and \(9\) m are scalars because no direction is included. \(9\) N east is a vector because force has a direction.

questions.prompt: A temperature changes from \(12^\circ\)C to \(19^\circ\)C. Calculate the scalar change.
questions.answer: Subtract final minus initial: \(19-12=7\). The scalar change is \(7^\circ\)C.

questions.prompt: A cyclist travels \(3\) km east then \(4\) km north. Find the total distance travelled and explain why it is scalar.
questions.answer: The distance travelled is \(3+4=7\) km. It is scalar because it records path length only, not direction.

questions.prompt: A force has magnitude \(15\) N and points west. Identify the scalar part and the vector information.
questions.answer: The scalar part is the magnitude \(15\) N. The direction west is what makes the force a vector.

questions.prompt: A lift rises from height \(2\) m to \(17\) m. Find the scalar height change and the upward displacement vector.
questions.answer: The scalar height change is \(17-2=15\) m. With upward positive, the displacement vector is \(+15\) m upward.

questions.prompt: A runner completes one \(400\) m lap and finishes where she started. Find distance travelled and displacement.
questions.answer: Distance is the path length, \(400\) m. Displacement is \(\mathbf0\), because the final and initial positions are the same.

questions.prompt: A box has mass \(8\) kg and weight \(78.4\) N downward. Identify the scalar and vector quantities.
questions.answer: Mass \(8\) kg is scalar. Weight is a force with direction downward, so it is a vector.

questions.prompt: A speedometer reads \(22\) m s\(^{-1}\), while velocity is \(22\) m s\(^{-1}\) south. Explain the mathematical difference.
questions.answer: Speed is the scalar magnitude \(22\) m s\(^{-1}\). Velocity includes that magnitude and the direction south, so it is a vector.

questions.prompt: A block moves along a line from \(x=-3\) m to \(x=5\) m. Find the scalar distance between the positions.
questions.answer: Distance on a line is absolute separation: \(|5-(-3)|=8\) m.

questions.prompt: A vector velocity is \((-6,8)\) m s\(^{-1}\). Find the scalar speed.
questions.answer: Speed is magnitude: \(\sqrt{(-6)^2+8^2}=10\) m s\(^{-1}\).

questions.prompt: A parcel is displaced by \((2,-1,2)\) m under a force of magnitude \(5\) N. Which given quantity is scalar and which is vector?
questions.answer: The displacement is a vector because it has components. The stated force magnitude \(5\) N is scalar because no direction is given.

questions.prompt: A scalar \(k=-3\) multiplies \(\mathbf v=(2,-5)\). Calculate \(k\mathbf v\) and describe the direction change.
questions.answer: Multiply components: \((-6,15)\). A negative scalar reverses direction, and the factor \(3\) triples the magnitude.

questions.prompt: A car travels \(50\) km north then \(50\) km south. Find scalar distance and vector displacement.
questions.answer: The scalar distance is \(100\) km. The vector displacement is \(\mathbf0\) because the two directed trips cancel.

questions.prompt: A displacement vector is \(\mathbf d=(5,12)\) m. Find the scalar distance from start to finish.
questions.answer: The straight-line distance is \(|\mathbf d|=\sqrt{25+144}=13\) m.

questions.prompt: A plane has ground velocity \(\mathbf v=(120,50)\) km h\(^{-1}\). Find the scalar speed.
questions.answer: The speed is \(|\mathbf v|=\sqrt{120^2+50^2}=130\) km h\(^{-1}\).

questions.prompt: An object has kinetic energy \(32\) J and momentum \(\mathbf p=(6,8,0)\) kg m s\(^{-1}\). Identify each type and find \(|\mathbf p|\).
questions.answer: Kinetic energy is scalar. Momentum is vector, and \(|\mathbf p|=\sqrt{36+64}=10\) kg m s\(^{-1}\).

questions.prompt: A one-dimensional velocity is \(-4\) m s\(^{-1}\). Find the scalar speed and the direction information.
questions.answer: The scalar speed is \(|-4|=4\) m s\(^{-1}\). The negative sign gives direction along the chosen axis.

questions.prompt: A force \(\mathbf F=(6,2)\) N moves an object by \(\mathbf s=(3,0)\) m, giving \(W=18\) J. Calculate the work and explain why the answer is scalar even though the inputs are vectors.
questions.answer: Compute \(W=\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf s=6\cdot3+2\cdot0=18\) J. The dot product outputs one number, not a direction-bearing vector, so work has magnitude and units but no direction. It is therefore scalar.

questions.prompt: A vector velocity \(\mathbf v=(a,4)\) m s\(^{-1}\) has scalar speed \(5\) m s\(^{-1}\). Find possible values of \(a\), then state the two possible directions qualitatively.
questions.answer: Speed is the magnitude of velocity, so \(a^2+4^2=5^2\). Hence \(a^2=9\), giving \(a=3\) or \(a=-3\). The two velocities are \((3,4)\) and \((-3,4)\): both have upward component \(4\), but one points to the right and the other to the left.

questions.prompt: A hiker walks \(2\) km east, \(2\) km north, \(2\) km west, and \(2\) km south, taking \(2\) hours in total. Find scalar distance, displacement, average speed, and average velocity.
questions.answer: The scalar distance is \(2+2+2+2=8\) km. The east-west and north-south components cancel, so displacement is \(\mathbf0\). Average speed is distance over time, \(8/2=4\) km h\(^{-1}\). Average velocity is displacement over time, \(\mathbf0/2=\mathbf0\) km h\(^{-1}\).
